correctness.rationale: Decompose a rank-r full-domain diagram α into a rank-r full transformation t mapping top kernel block A_i to a selected b_i in lower through-block B_i, then a rank-r diagram idempotent e with top blocks D_1=B_1 union lower-only blocks C_j and D_i=B_i (i>1), retaining B_i and C_j bottom partitions. Diagram multiplication gives α=te and e²=e. Transformations t factor as a kernel idempotent followed by vacancy moves of r labelled image tokens through n positions; each vacancy move is a rank-r idempotent fixing its image. This proves exact rank preservation, and excluding rank-n units is essential. Independently inspected exhaustive n<=5 diagram verifier and reasoned through the general token-move construction; finite cases are secondary.
residual_risks: The argument depends on the explicit stated hypotheses; no unproved extension is claimed.

evidence: Carroll, East and Fresacher, Presentations for semigroups of full-domain partitions (arXiv:2507.05497): Theorem 3.16 gives idempotent generation of the largest singular ideal; no explicit exact-rank factorization for every lower ideal found in inspected theorem.
East and Gray, Ehresmann theory and partition monoids (arXiv:2011.00663): The prior question targets proper rank ideals; it does not itself solve uniform rank-r factors.

East and Gray, Diagram monoids and Graham–Houghton graphs: idempotents and generating sets of ideals (arXiv:1404.2359): Unrestricted partition monoid generators cannot automatically remain inside the full-domain submonoid or at the precise rank.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Full partition monoid ideal generation has larger ambient algebra but its generators may leave the full-domain submonoid. Carroll–East–Fresacher largest singular ideal theorem is a weaker set-theoretic target than all proper ideals.
